issues.body: `_upload_could_include` compares the unresolved YAML `path:` text directly with the relative target. An upload such as `path: ${{ github.workspace }}` or `path: ${{ github.workspace }}/coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` retains the runner-root log after Actions expression expansion but returns false here. Absolute workspace paths are also reduced only by stripping `/`, leaving a workspace prefix that cannot match the relative target. Thus a common broad upload can still be introduced while the promised regression test stays green.
issues.fix_hint: Conservatively reject upload path entries containing unresolved GitHub expressions or absolute paths unless they can be normalized relative to the known workspace, and add negative fixtures for `${{ github.workspace }}`, `${{ github.workspace }}/coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json`, and an absolute workspace directory. Alternatively, write the log into a dedicated directory and reject any upload specification that is broad, dynamic, or can include that directory.
issues.title: Artifact matcher misses expression-based and absolute workspace paths

verdict.summary: Round 2 corrects the evidence-base description and substantially improves wildcard/directory coverage, resolving the first prior finding and narrowing the second. However, the retention invariant is still bypassable through GitHub-expression or absolute upload paths, even though those resolve to the same workspace file at runtime. The targeted test could not be executed in this checkout because PyYAML is unavailable; the defect follows directly from the matcher implementation.
